Research notes, Take Your Mark.

Created because the Meet Manager article names it among supported timers.

A naming trap, and the reason this page opens the way it does. "Take your mark" is also the

mostly starting procedure, not this company. Two pages here use the phrase in that sense,

Search for the abbreviation TYM alongside it.

What is established, from Hy-Tek's Meet Manager 8 guide
(hytek.active.com/user_guides_html/swmm8/takeyourmark.htm, read September 2026): Meet
Manager reaches the Take Your Mark console, abbreviated TYM in that documentation, through
Hy-Tek's Generic Interface using file sharing rather than a cable. Race results move from
the console into a file in the Meet Manager database directory with no keying. The console
is also in the group that can accept an event schedule downloaded from Meet Manager, which
not all of them can, and Hy-Tek writes a generic.sch schedule file for it.

So it belongs with IST and Wylas as a network or file-sharing system rather than a serial
one.

Still to research: who makes it and where; what the console is as hardware; when it
appeared; and whether TYM is the product name, the company name or both.

This article is a stub. Take Your Mark, abbreviated TYM in Hy-Tek's documentation, is a
swimming timing console that [Meet Manager](../software/hy-tek-meet-manager.md) reaches
through a shared file rather than a cable, with race results landing directly in the
program's database directory.

It is one of the minority of consoles that will also accept an event schedule sent down
from the meet software; see the [vendors](index.md) register for the companies this wiki
covers.
